rv.q: This is not your typical overblown West End musical – and is all the better for it.
Not a resounding triumph, perhaps, but many aspects are bound to resonate.
The truth is, though, that the years have been kinder to Ball than they have been to Aspects.

For example, the leading man Alex’s creepy infatuation with a young girl, who’s now older, at 18. (It’s still queasy, though.) The show explores, over a 20-year post-war period, love’s vario us aspects - especially the horizontal. Jamie Bogyo is the dull but handsome Alex, the young lover of actress Rose (Laura Pitt-Pulford, a total pro).
But really it would probably be easier for everyone if this is the last time we try to rehabilitate this thing.
And the whole thing feels off, like a day-old fish.
We get the sense that these people could only ever exist within the bounds of a musical – one that is easy enough to watch but entirely unconvincing in its emotions.
But you sit through the two and a half hours hoping that the characters will acquire some sort of depth.
What a gooey, oozy, gaudy box of stale chocolates this is.

sg.ra: Closest and most direct view of the stage at Lyric Theatre, with the fullest sound. The standard top pick for any show here.
An elevated, full-stage view with no orchestra-level neck-craning — especially strong for shows with big staging or choreography.
A modest side angle on the stage but still close and clear — a reliable choice when center seats are sold out.

sg.vl: Good sound, check the seat map
sg.ra: Lyric Theatre's own seating notes flag possible obstructed views from the rear orchestra — sound still carries well, but check the seat map before booking here.
At 1,930 seats, Lyric Theatre is one of the larger Broadway houses — far side mezzanine seats sit well off-axis and a long way from the stage.

vs.sum: One of Broadway's largest houses (1,930 seats across four levels), the Lyric's sheer scale means rear orchestra and mezzanine seats sit far from the stage, with sightline obstructions from balcony overhangs. Acoustics are solid and the theater's modern construction makes it well-suited for spectacle productions.

acc.note: 42nd St entrance at street level with elevator to Orchestra and Dress Circle. No elevator to Balcony.
